atoms.b: In 1939, the Second World War began, and the United Kingdom was at ((++war peace)) with Germany.
Germany had a special machine called the Enigma. It produced a code that was too difficult for even the ((++smartest dumbest)) people in the UK to solve.

feedback.finish: Alan led a team of mathematicians during the war in Hut 8 at Bletchley Park. They worked on breaking enigma codes.

instruction.text: Let’s do some code breaking! don’t worry it won’t be as difficult as what Alan Turing worked on.

hint.text: Look at the image, it will help you work out what letter each number corresponds to.

atoms.a: What is the secret word in the sequence: 5 14 9 7 13 1?
atoms.sound: What is the secret word in the sequence: 5, 14, 9, 7, 13, 1?
Eventually, Alan helped to create something called the Bombe machine.
This machine was able to decode enigma messages.

text: This massively helped the war effort as the British could work out what the Nazis were planning. Throughout the war, 211 of these Bombe machines were built!

feedback.finish: In 1946, Alan received a special award called an OBE for his wartime work of cracking the enigma code.
